Card 4.0 / Community guide

Bring the card to your community.

Start with one merchant and a few cards. This guide takes your federation from choosing a till to settling its first sale.

Two ways to get cards

Get ready-made cards

Pilot communities can order cards at cost, set up for their federation and shipped to them. Tell us which federation you use and how many people will take part.

Ask about pilot cards

Set up your own cards

Start with compatible blank cards such as the J3R180 or J3R452. Your issuer uses the Setup app on an NFC phone to prepare a batch for your federation.

Find blank cards

Your pilot kit

Start with one merchant. Agree who will run the till and who will issue cards before you hand out the first one.

Federation
Your guardians run a Fedimint federation with a bitcoin mint v1 or v2. It holds the bitcoin and settles payments.
Merchant till
The till runs on a server and receives sales into its own federation wallet. The operator installs the Card 4.0 till and backs up its wallet and records.
Merchant phone
Each merchant pairs the POS app on an NFC phone with the till. The phone reads balances, loads cards and takes payments.
Cards & issuer phone
Each holder gets a card and PIN. The issuer uses Card Setup on an NFC phone to prepare blank cards and approve tills.
Card registry
Ask the registry operator for a Setup account. Setup and the till must use the same Card 4.0 registry, and the cards and till must match on federation and mint.

Your first sale

Walk through a small payment together. Open each step as you go.

  1. Connect and approve the till

    Join your federation from the till, then connect it to the Card 4.0 registry your issuer uses. In Setup, open Settings › Tills › Add a till and follow the prompts using the QR or short code shown by the till.

  2. Pair a merchant’s phone

    Show the till’s POS pairing QR. On the merchant’s phone, open POS settings and choose Pair with till. Keep the phone online and confirm it has fetched an offline kit before testing an offline sale.

  3. Give the holder a card and PIN

    Use a ready-made card or tap a blank card in Setup. Each card creates its keys on the chip. Give the holder their card and its PIN of 4 to 8 digits.

  4. Top up the card

    Read the card in POS, choose Top up card, enter an amount in sats and tap Review top-up. Check the card credit, fee and total. Choose Show payment QR, pay the Lightning invoice once, then tap the card to load the quoted amount.

  5. Take a payment

    In POS, choose Charge card and enter the price. The holder enters their PIN on the merchant’s phone and taps the card. Check the result on the phone before starting another sale.

  6. Reconcile the day’s sales

    Reconnect any phones used offline so queued payments can settle. Check the sales and wallet balance in till admin, confirm the phones have finished syncing, and follow the backup instructions for your till.

Costs & card care

What to budget for

Allow for one card per holder, a server for the till, and NFC phones for merchants and the issuer. See the card buying guide for example prices.

A new till can start with an empty wallet. Each top-up quotes a fixed fee to cover receiving the Lightning payment and loading the card. Any fee left after costs stays with the merchant. The sending wallet may charge a routing fee.

What holders should know

For this experimental pilot, carry only amounts you can afford to lose. A lost or wiped card loses its eCash. Keep your PIN private and enter it only at a till you trust.

The registry can see card balances. Load the card through POS. The Fedi wallet app cannot write a top-up to the card. Read about card privacy.

What merchants should know

The apps are in beta. The notes on a card limit which amounts it can pay. Top-ups round to amounts the card can hold, so check the quoted credit with the holder.

Offline sales settle after the phone reconnects. The project’s pilot risk guide covers settlement and the limits of testing.

Help with your pilot

For cards or questions about getting started, write to hi@fedimintcard.org.
